cohort: 2500 patients who underwent cesarean section at a tertiary-level university hospital in Oman from January 2015 to December 2019
finding: While general anesthesia is associated with better hemodynamic stability during cesarean section compared to regional anesthesia, it also leads to a higher risk of significant blood loss and lower APGAR scores.
mod_finding: This study comparing general anesthesia (GA) and regional anesthesia (RA) for cesarean section found that while GA had better hemodynamic stability, RA resulted in less blood loss and higher APGAR scores.
